On the day of the extraction, it was still painful, swollen, and inflamed, but the dentist insisted it could be done, saying it wouldn't be painful with local anesthesia. So I decided to go ahead. After the anesthesia was injected, the dentist started, and in less than three minutes, I screamed because it was incredibly painful. It was excruciatingly painful, like there was no anesthesia at all. My arms and legs were shaking, my hands were numb, and I was breathing rapidly. The dentist couldn't continue and told me to rest for about 10 minutes. I sat there crying, my arms, legs, and hands shaking and numb. After that, he forced himself to finish the procedure, which was incredibly agonizing (imagine what it's like to have a tooth extracted without anesthesia). But the dentist said I was panicking and afraid of him because it was my first time at the dentist, which wasn't true at all. It was pure pain. I can't even describe the pain. My arms, legs, and hands were shaking and numb. You've studied dentistry, you should know how painful it is. Teeth are incredibly delicate. It was the most agonizing experience of my life.

They said the anesthetic wouldn't reach it if they gave it to me. And yes, it was incredibly painful, just like the anesthetic didn't work at all, as I mentioned. At the hospital, they would have given me medication to take to reduce the swelling and inflammation first.
